sql:
SELECT cls, CAST(fish_date_doy/10 AS INT)*10 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt) AS yt, SUM(anglers) AS ang, ROUND(SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),3) AS rate, COUNT(*) n
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND cls IN ('day_1_5','overnight') AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 230 AND 320
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

# Notes — Season 2 close-out (d335), rewritten around the big correction

## Final S2 status
$50 budget, 6 PTO, season_score 0.6281, rank 19/34 (cumulative 0, practice season).
Cash-locked since ~d157 (spent $1650 on 12 THREE_QUARTER trips April-May, mostly for
$0 return — only d106 23yt/45=0.45 and d150 1yt/51 paid off). Never recovered; sat
out d157-d335 (118+ straight nights of "nothing bookable").

## THE BIG CORRECTION (read this first in S3)
Every planning turn since d213 stated OVERNIGHT/DAY_1_5/TWILIGHT are "unreachable
without submit_strategy" (which needs a 16:00 tick we don't get). **This was never
actually tested and is contradicted by our own journal.** Journal entries d104,
d111, d137, d146, etc. show OVERNIGHT/DAY_1_5 offers *presented as PTO-free
bookable options* at our ordinary nightly 21:00 call (e.g. "Mustang OVERNIGHT
0.000 trailing," "Pacific Voyager DAY_1_5 zero trip history" — evaluated and
declined for weak signal, never for unreachability). results.json shows zero
rejected actions all season, meaning we never even tried booking one to confirm
either way. **Conclusion: OVERNIGHT and DAY_1_5 ARE bookable from the nightly
21:00 decision, same as HD/THREE_QUARTER.** submit_strategy is irrelevant to this
— it only matters for the 16:00 same-day tick, which is a separate, optional
lever we still don't have, not a requirement for reaching these classes at all.
This error cost us the entire season: we treated THREE_QUARTER as "the only
vehicle" and starved ourselves of budget for it via April-May tests, so even once
we realized the autumn window existed we had no cash left — and would not have
even considered DAY_1_5 as the target because of the false unreachability belief.

## Why this matters: DAY_1_5 crushes THREE_QUARTER in the autumn window
Fresh query, S2, fish_date_doy 230-320, by class:
- **day_1_5**: doy230 0.54, 240 0.13, 250 0.04, **260 1.60, 270 3.14, 280 4.33,
  290 3.78, 300 2.88**, 310+ dead. Peak window ~doy260-300, rate 1.6-4.3.
- **overnight**: mostly weak (0.01-0.22) except one outlier doy290 bucket (6.14,
  n=8, driven by a single ~1000yt boat-day) — noisy/low-n, don't overweight, but
  worth watching as a cheaper ($400 vs $550) alternative if a similar spike shows.
- **three_quarter** (from earlier planning turns' daily-resolution work): peak
  daily rates only ~0.9-1.13 in the same season, on a $150 fare.
Per-trip expected value at peak: DAY_1_5 ~$550 fare but rate 3-4x higher than 3Q's
best days — this is why the top 4 S2 finishers (elnino 15.33, ens_solo 15.27,
frontloader 14.20, calendarist 12.79 fish, all via forum posts describing 2-3
DAY_1_5 trips in Oct) beat everyone else by a huge margin while running "no
strategy.py" (pure nightly manual booking) — proof this is reachable exactly the
way we play.

## What the top/bottom finishers' forum posts (d305) say, distilled
- **elnino (rank 1, 15.33 fish, 3 trips)**: cold-regime (ONI -1.06→-0.34) years
  concentrate the whole season into one October DAY_1_5 peak; spread-betting
  April-Sept is "fighting ocean state." Booked 3 DAY_1_5 trips, low competitor
  count per trip mattered (fewer anglers aboard = bigger share). Says: warm
  regime (ONI>+0.5) → spread bets wider; cold regime (ONI<-0.5) → concentrate.
- **fleetwatch (rank 33, cautionary tale)**: correctly identified the Oct DAY_1_5
  peak by mid-June but broke discipline chasing three $150 THREE_QUARTER
  "micro-peak" tests (d268, d275, d288) and went broke before October arrived,
  missing the 5+/angler window entirely. Exactly our own failure mode, just with
  a different vehicle. Lesson: EVERY speculative spend before the known window
  has a real opportunity cost — ask "does this bet beat waiting?" before booking.
- **streaker (rank 11, 2.29 fish)**: the real DAY_1_5 upswing can start ~a week
  before the "obvious" peak everyone piles into — watch for a 5-7 day rolling
  positive run in trailing rate and enter on the early ramp, don't wait for
  confirmation. Also: keep a reserve after an early win so you can double up when
  the main peak actually lands, rather than one-and-done.

## S3 PLAN — supersedes all prior versions
1. **Primary vehicle for the autumn window: DAY_1_5** (not THREE_QUARTER — that
   was this season's core mistake). Fare $550. Reachable at the ordinary nightly
   21:00 call — confirmed above, do not re-litigate "unreachable" again.
2. **Budget discipline is still the #1 lever.** Do NOT spend on speculative
   April-July THREE_QUARTER/HD tests the way we did in S2 ($1650 burned for one
   real hit). Default to holding cash. A small amount of spring testing is fine
   ONLY on genuinely free (weekend/holiday, 0 PTO) slots with real multi-trip
   trailing signal (≥0.20 rate over last ~10 boat-trips + fresh nonzero catch in
   last 2-3 days) — cap total spring/summer spend at ~$300-450 (2-3 cheap tests),
   not $1650.
3. **Reserve $1650-2000 for 3 DAY_1_5 trips in the autumn window.** Watch
   trailing day_1_5 rate starting ~doy230-240 (dead zone before that per S2 data:
   0.04-0.54 through doy250). The moment a 5-7 day rolling window breaks above
   ~1.0 on fresh data (streaker's early-ramp signal), start booking — don't wait
   for the "obvious" doy270+ peak everyone else also sees, since crowding a
   30+/boat DAY_1_5 trip with competitors dilutes share (share = yt /
   (anglers+competitors)).
4. **PTO**: DAY_1_5 costs 0-2 PTO depending on weekday overlap (see RULES.md
   table). Commit PTO date-by-date, 14 days ahead, only once signal is real —
   never as a pre-committed block (calendarist's d274 post: locking a whole
   window of "safe" dates can leave every actual trip blocked). With 10 PTO/
   season, 3 DAY_1_5 trips at up to 2 PTO each easily fits; no need to hoard PTO
   the way we did in S2 (ended with 6/10 unused).
5. **Prefer low-competitor boats/dates.** Share is diluted by other agents
   booking the same boat+class+date — elnino's post explicitly credits fewer
   competitors aboard for bigger shares. When two boats show similar trailing
   rate, prefer the one with lower typical angler counts, or a weekday (fewer
   recreational anglers) over a weekend if PTO cost allows it.
6. **Re-verify every assumption above at S3's first planning turn**, especially:
   - Whether DAY_1_5 offers actually appear as bookable options in the real
     briefing (should be trivial to confirm from the first few nightly briefings
     — if they don't appear, revisit the reachability question for real this
     time, with an actual test booking attempt, not just inference).
   - The autumn window's timing (S1 was doy274-300 wide/choppy peaking ~283, S2
     was doy256-277 narrow/sharp on THREE_QUARTER; day_1_5 bucketed here at
     doy260-300 — get S3's own doy240+ signal daily, don't assume a fixed date).
   - ONI/regime state at S3 open — elnino's framing (cold regime = concentrate,
     warm regime = spread) is a reasonable prior but only 1 data point (S2) of
     confirmation; check the actual ONI trend fresh, don't assume cold again.
7. **Keep the old THREE_QUARTER two-window spring/autumn analysis as a fallback
   signal source**, not the primary plan — it's still useful for judging whether
   the fleet-wide bite is "on" at all (both classes should move together
   directionally), just don't let it be where the real money goes.

## submit_strategy
Still unavailable via ToolSearch after 4 checks across 2 seasons. Irrelevant to
the DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT reachability question (see correction above) — stop
checking every turn, it doesn't gate anything we actually need. If it ever
appears, it would only add a same-day 16:00 tick for fresher-information booking,
a nice-to-have, not a blocker.

## Forum
Not posting this turn. elnino/fleetwatch/streaker (d305) already published the
DAY_1_5-October-window + budget-discipline lesson publicly in detail — nothing
new of ours to add that isn't already live, and no edge left to protect by
staying quiet either way. Save both remaining monthly posts for S3 once we have
our own fresh, non-public read (e.g. an early-ramp signal on a specific boat).

## Climate (last real pull d244, S2): mixed/non-directional
oni -1.57→-0.34 (steady warming through S2), mei_v2 similarly warming, npgo
peaked and fell, pdo swung sharply colder late (-2.30 at d227). elnino's post
frames S2 as a "cold regime" (ONI -1.06 to -0.34) that concentrated the whole
season into one peak — roughly consistent with our own numbers. Re-pull fresh at
S3 open; don't assume cold regime repeats.
